title: Advanced pronouns and placement
objectives: I can place object pronouns correctly in formal Portuguese using enclisis, proclisis and mesoclisis, and say which word in the sentence decides the position.
I can write attached pronouns correctly, including the accents and the forms lo, la, no and na (fazê-lo, compraram-no, informá-la-emos).
I can recognize combined pronouns such as mo, to and lho in formal and literary texts and replace them in everyday speech.
I can identify and use the different roles of se: reflexive, reciprocal, passive, impersonal, inherent and emphatic.
I can place pronouns with ir plus infinitive and with compound tenses, in both formal and colloquial Brazilian usage.

vocabulary.note: A pronominal verb is a verb used with a pronoun that points back to the subject (here se). In arrepender-se the pronoun is part of the verb: arrepender alone does not exist. The rr between vowels is the strong r, said like a breathy English h: a-he-pen-DER-si. The thing regretted follows de. The same verb also means to repent in a religious sense.

example.target: Arrependo-me de não ter estudado mais.
example.source: I regret not having studied more.
example.source_literal: I-regret-myself of not to-have studied more.

vocabulary.note: More formal than reclamar, which takes no se. The thing complained about follows de. Spelling: qu before e is k (the u is silent), ei is one diphthong beat and x after ei is sh, so the word is said kay-SHAR-si.

example.source: The residents complained about the noise.

vocabulary.note: Without se, dirigir means to direct or to drive a car. With se it means to turn oneself toward someone or something: to speak to a person or to go to a place. In the formal command dirija-se the g becomes j, because g before a would be the hard g of go, and j keeps the zh sound.

To bind oneself by a promise; the promise follows a plus infinitive. Without se, comprometer means to compromise in the sense of to endanger (comprometer a segurança), which is not the English sense of reaching a compromise. The m before p marks a nasal vowel: kõ-pro-me-TER-si.

example.target: Comprometo-me a entregar o relatório na segunda.
example.source: I commit to delivering the report on Monday.
example.source_literal: I-commit-myself to deliver the report on-the Monday.

vocabulary.note: Lembrar without se means to remind someone of something, and in casual speech it is also used for to remember. The pronominal form with de is the careful one. In daquele, de and aquele fuse into one word.
Pronominal verb that is used with se in standard speech and writing. The action dared follows a plus infinitive.
Fixed expression built from dar and conta (account, reckoning): to give oneself an account of something, hence to notice it. Spoken Portuguese often uses perceber for the same idea.

example.target: Dei-me conta do erro tarde demais.
example.source: I realized the mistake too late.
example.source_literal: I-gave-myself account of-the mistake late too-much.

vocabulary.note: Two uses. With a plural subject it is reciprocal: people find each other, which is to meet. With a singular subject that is a thing it is a formal substitute for estar: the thing finds itself somewhere. Encontramo-nos is encontramos with its final s dropped before nos.

example.source: We meet at eight in the square.

vocabulary.note: A reciprocal verb describes an action that each member of a plural subject does to the others. False friend: cumprimentar means to greet, not to compliment, which is elogiar.

example.target: Os colegas cumprimentaram-se com um aperto de mão.
example.source: The colleagues greeted each other with a handshake.
example.source_literal: The colleagues greeted-themselves with a squeeze of hand.

vocabulary.note: Mutuamente or uns aos outros removes any doubt between the reciprocal and the reflexive reading, since os vizinhos se ajudam could also mean that each neighbor helps himself.
With a plural subject it means to understand each other or to get along; entender-se com alguém is to sort things out with someone.

example.target: Eles se entendem sem precisar falar.
example.source: They understand each other without having to speak.
example.source_literal: They themselves understand without needing to-speak.

vocabulary.note: Formal way to say that an event happens: the event carries itself out. False friend: realizar means to carry out or to make real, not to realize in the sense of understanding, which is dar-se conta.

example.source: The hearing will take place on Friday.

vocabulary.note: A written request addressed to an authority, from requerer, to request formally. Pedido is the everyday word for request. The person who files it is o requerente or a requerente: nouns ending in -nte have one form for both genders and the article shows the gender.

example.target: O requerimento foi entregue na prefeitura.
example.source: The application was handed in at the city hall.
example.source_literal: The application was handed-in at-the prefecture.

vocabulary.note: Administrative and legal verb, and a false friend: it does not mean to defer or postpone. It conjugates like preferir (eu defiro). The first syllable is said ji in many accents: d before an i sound is said like the j of judge, and in relaxed speech an unstressed e at the start of a word is often said i.
The prefix in- is negative, as in English indecisive, so this is the opposite of deferir. Like deferir it conjugates like preferir.

example.source: The city hall rejected the application.

vocabulary.note: The period of time allowed for doing something, so also the time limit. A single z between vowels is said z: PRA-zu.

example.target: O prazo para a entrega termina na sexta.
example.source: The deadline for delivery ends on Friday.

vocabulary.note: False friend. English protocol means a set of rules or procedures; in Brazilian bureaucracy o protocolo is the stamped receipt and its number, given to you when you file a request. It is stressed on the second to last syllable (pro-to-KO-lo), so no accent is written.

example.target: Guarde o número do protocolo para consultar o processo.
example.source: Keep the reference number to check on the case.

vocabulary.note: To inform someone officially, usually in writing. With the pronoun o it becomes notificá-lo: the r drops and the stress ends up on the last syllable.

example.source: We will notify him in writing.

vocabulary.note: The office of an organization that receives complaints from the public, from ouvir, to hear. The stressed i is on the second to last syllable, which a final a predicts, so no accent is written (compare padaria).

example.target: A ouvidoria recebeu a queixa dos moradores.
example.source: The ombudsman's office received the residents' complaint.

lines.source: Bruno, can you help me with this letter? I have to write to the bank and I don't know where to put the pronouns.
lines.source_literal: Bruno, me you-help with this letter? I-have that to-write to the bank and not I-know where to-place the pronouns.

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.target: Na fala a gente diz me dá uma resposta, mas numa carta se escreve dê-me uma resposta.
lines.source: In speech we say me dá uma resposta, but in a letter you write dê-me uma resposta.

lines.source_literal: And if the sentence should-have a word negative, type não?

lines.speaker: Sofia

dialogues.title: Reunião de condomínio
dialogues.context: Neighbors meet to discuss noise complaints and a planned barbecue. Several uses of se appear naturally.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.target: Alguns moradores queixam-se do som alto depois das dez, e ninguém sabe a quem se dirigir.

lines.source_literal: Some residents complain-themselves of-the sound loud after of-the ten, and nobody knows to whom oneself to-direct.

lines.speaker: Tavares

grammar.title: Spelling and sound: the words of this unit
grammar.explanation:
This note applies the method from the stress lesson to the new words of this unit, so that no spelling is left unexplained. The method never changes. Divide the word into syllables, find the stressed syllable by ear, read the default stress from the ending, and compare. If the stress agrees with the default, no accent is written. If it disagrees, the stressed vowel carries an accent: acute for an open vowel, circumflex for a closed one. A written accent is therefore never decoration; it says that this word breaks the default of its ending.

Three facts are specific to this unit. First, a pronoun written after a verb is joined to it by a hyphen, but it is still a clitic, which is an unstressed word that leans on a neighboring word. It adds a weak syllable at the end and never moves the stress, so disse-me is DIS-si-mi, stressed on the verb. The weak-vowel rule from the sound lesson applies to the pronoun: a final unstressed e is said i and a final unstressed o is said u, so me is mi, se is si, o is u, and lhe is lyi (lh is the ly of million). Second, when a pronoun is attached, the verb itself can change its spelling (fazê-lo, encontramo-nos, informá-la-emos). That is a separate rule, and the third note of this unit explains it. Third, the unit is full of words from law and administration. They are regular, but their spellings are easy to misread, and the table gives each group with its reason.

Two reminders cover most of the table. A vowel followed by m or n and then a consonant is nasal: the m or n is not said as a consonant, and m is written before b and p while n is written before every other consonant (lembrar, comprometer, entender). And d before an i sound is said like the j of judge, which combines with the relaxed unstressed first-syllable e (often said i), so deferir usually begins with the sound ji. The last row of the table points ahead to the accents and hyphens of attached pronouns.

headers: Why they are written this way
rows: rr between vowels writes the strong r, a breathy h as in English hat. en before d marks a nasal vowel. The hyphen joins the clitic, which adds a weak syllable and does not move the stress.

qu before e or i is k and the u is silent. ei is a diphthong, one beat. x after ei is sh. Word-initial r is the strong r. Final unstressed e is said i, and t before that i is ch. Esquecerei ends in the diphthong ei, which is stressed by default.

g before e or i is zh. Before a, g would be the hard g of go, so the command is spelled with j (dirija), which keeps the zh sound. j is always zh. d before an i sound is said like the j of judge (written jee in the last column).

d before an i sound is said like the j of judge, and an unstressed first-syllable e is often said i, so de- is usually ji. n before d marks a nasal vowel. The ending r makes the last syllable the stressed one by default.
lembrar-se, comprometer-se, cumprimentar-se, encontrar-se, entender-se, emprestei

m or n after a vowel and before a consonant marks a nasal vowel: m before b and p, n elsewhere. These infinitives end in r and emprestei ends in the diphthong ei, so all of them default to the last syllable and need no accent.
lẽ-BRAR-si, kõ-pro-me-TER-si, kũ-pri-mẽ-TAR-si, ẽ-kõ-TRAR-si, ẽ-tẽ-DER-si, ẽ-pres-TAY
gu before e or i keeps the hard g of go, because g alone would be zh: this is the change that -gar verbs make in the eu form of the preterite. ch is sh.

A word ending in a is stressed on the second to last syllable by default. These are stressed on the last syllable, so the open a takes an acute. In the simple future the third person singular ending is always written á.

ou is a diphthong, one beat, said close to the o of go. In ouvidoria the stressed i is on the second to last syllable, which a final a predicts, so no accent is written (compare padaria). In prefeitura, ei is a diphthong and the stress is on tu.
agência, audiência, experiência, notícia, rodoviária, relatório, condomínio, cópias, crédito, jurídicos

These are stressed on the third to last syllable, because a final ia, io or ea counts as two vowels, so no ending predicts the stress and the accent is always written. Open vowels take the acute (notícia, relatório, crédito); a closed e before a nasal consonant takes the circumflex (agência, experiência). t before i is ch, d before i is j, c before o is k and j is zh.
a-ZHEN-sya, au-ji-EN-sya, es-pe-ri-EN-sya, no-CHEE-sya, ho-do-vi-AH-rya, he-la-TO-ryu, kõ-do-MEE-nyu, KO-pyas, KRE-ji-tu, zhu-REE-ji-kus
Proparoxytones, so the accent is always written: closed e in ên-, open o in pró- and mesó-. s between vowels is z. In oblíquo the u after q is pronounced, because qu before o is kw.
The second to last syllable is the default for a final o or a, so no accent is written. Double ss between vowels writes s, while a single z between vowels is z. c before a is k, and t before i is ch.

l at the end of a syllable is said w, so balcão begins with bau. gu before a is g plus w: the u is pronounced. x before t is said s. The hyphen joins the two parts of a compound, and each part keeps its own stress.
nh is the ny of canyon and lh is the ly of million. Neither h is said on its own.
ç is the s sound before a, o or u and never begins a word. s between vowels is z (revisão), and so is z between vowels (duzentos).

reunião is re-u-ni-ÃO: e and u are two beats, and ão is stressed on the last syllable by default. Neste is em plus este and daquele is de plus aquele, because a preposition fuses with a demonstrative as in the contractions lesson. Nem ends in the nasal em.
cigarro, encerra, recorrer, ribeiro, corrige, registrado, vossa
rr between vowels is the strong r, and so is a word-initial r (ribeiro). g before e or i is zh (corrige, registrado). ss between vowels is a plain s. c before i is s. ei is a diphthong, one beat.
si-GA-hu, ẽ-SE-ha, he-ko-HER, hi-BAY-ru, ko-HEE-zhi, he-zhis-TRA-du, VO-sa

nh is the ny of canyon. c before e is s. The ending em (with or without s) defaults to the second to last syllable, so conhecem is said ko-NYE-sẽy. Senhoria and soaria are stressed on the i before the final a, which a final a predicts once ia counts as two vowels, so no accent is written (compare ouvidoria).

qu before e is k, and the spelling is qu because c before e would be s (comunicar changes to comunique as -gar changes to -gue). An e at the start of a word followed by x and a vowel writes x as z (examine). x before a consonant is said s (textos, like sexta). ção becomes ções in the plural: the cedilla stays because the next letter is o, and õe is the nasal diphthong, stressed on the last syllable by default.

Proparoxytones, so the accent is always written. Gramática has an open stressed a. In espontânea the final ea counts as two vowels, and the closed stressed â sits before the nasal n, as in câmera, so the word is es-pon-TÂ-ne-a.
The accents and hyphens that appear when a pronoun is attached to a verb follow their own rules, which the third note sets out.

grammar.title: Enclisis, proclisis and mesoclisis
grammar.explanation:
A clitic pronoun is a short word with no stress of its own that leans on a verb and is said as part of it (the reflexive and object pronoun lessons introduced the term). Because it must lean, there is a question English never asks: on which side of the verb does it go? English object pronouns always follow the verb (tell me, give it to him). Portuguese has three positions. Proclisis puts the pronoun before the verb (me disse). Enclisis puts it after the verb, joined by a hyphen (disse-me). Mesoclisis puts it inside the verb, between two of its parts (dar-lhe-ei). The choice depends on the register, meaning the level of formality of the situation, and on what stands in front of the verb.

Spoken Brazilian Portuguese settled the question almost entirely one way: proclisis, even at the start of a sentence (Me dá um cigarro, Te vejo amanhã, Me disse que vinha). In speech, enclisis sounds formal and mesoclisis sounds like a legal document. The written standard follows a stricter rule inherited from European Portuguese, and you need it for two reasons: contracts, letters, exams and the press apply it, and you must be able to read it even if you never speak it.

The rule is built on a default and a list of exceptions. The default is enclisis: when the verb comes first in its clause, the pronoun leans back on it, so Disse-me a verdade, Encontramo-nos às oito, Dirijo-me ao senhor. (Formal writing forbids beginning a sentence with a clitic, which is exactly why the pronoun has to trail a verb that stands first.) The exceptions are words that stand before the verb and pull the pronoun forward. Traditional grammars call them attractors. They are words that carry stress or open a new clause: negative words (não, nunca, ninguém, nada, jamais, nem); subordinating conjunctions, which are the words that open a dependent clause (que, se, quando, embora, porque, caso); relative pronouns and question words (que, quem, onde, como); some adverbs (já, também, sempre, ainda, só, talvez); and indefinite words such as tudo, todos and alguém. With an attractor, the pronoun goes directly in front of the verb: Não me disse nada, Espero que me diga, Quem lhe disse isso?

Two details prevent most mistakes. First, an attractor affects only the clause it belongs to. In Se o pedido for indeferido, informá-la-emos, the se belongs to the first clause, and the main clause after the comma has no attractor, so it takes mesoclisis. Second, an ordinary subject is not an attractor in the strict European rule (Ela disse-me), but Brazilian writing accepts and usually prefers proclisis after a subject (Ela me disse, O gerente lhe informou), so both appear in good Brazilian texts. Coordinating conjunctions such as e, mas and ou do not attract: Comprei o livro e entreguei-o ontem.

Mesoclisis is possible in only two tenses, the simple future and the conditional, and the reason is their history. As the future lesson explained, these tenses began as the whole infinitive plus a form of haver (falar hei became falarei). The word is still two pieces joined together, so the pronoun can sit at the seam: dar-lhe-ei is dar plus lhe plus ei, and dir-se-ia is dir plus se plus ia (dizer loses its ze in these tenses, as it does in the plain future). There is a hyphen on each side of the pronoun. With an attractor the pronoun goes in front and the tense stays whole: Não lhe darei. Modern writers use mesoclisis rarely, mostly in law, in formal letters and in set phrases such as dir-se-ia (one would say) and tratar-se-á de (it will be a matter of). Most people avoid it by rephrasing with ir plus infinitive (Vou enviar-lhe) or with the present.

grammar.title: Spelling and sound: what happens to a verb when a pronoun is attached
grammar.explanation:
An attached pronoun produces a written compound of two parts joined by a hyphen: a verb form and a pronoun. The procedure has three steps. First, write the verb form exactly as it would be written alone, which fixes any accent by the default stress rule. Second, attach the pronoun. Third, check the three special cases below, in which the spelling of one of the two parts changes.

Case one: me, te, lhe, lhes, se and nos attach unchanged: disse-me, deu-lhe, queixaram-se. The one adjustment concerns nos. The verb form for we ends in -mos, and that s is dropped before nos, so encontramos plus nos is encontramo-nos and vemos plus nos is vemo-nos.

Case two: o, a, os and as become lo, la, los and las after a verb form that ends in r, s or z, and that final letter disappears: fazemos plus o is fazemo-lo, fiz plus o is fi-lo. The infinitive loses its r in the same way, and this leaves the stress on the last syllable, so the ordinary stress rule now demands an accent: the word is an oxytone ending in a or e, which the default does not predict. The vowel decides the mark. An -ar infinitive leaves a stressed open a, so the acute (notificar plus o is notificá-lo). An -er infinitive leaves a closed e, so the circumflex (fazer plus o is fazê-lo, ver plus o is vê-lo, ter plus o is tê-lo, contradizer plus o is contradizê-lo), and pôr gives pô-lo. An -ir infinitive leaves a stressed i, which needs no accent (abrir plus a is abri-la). The accent therefore belongs to the written compound and exists because the shortened verb is a new word with a new ending.

Case three: after a verb form that ends in a nasal sound, written m, ão or õe, the pronouns o, a, os and as become no, na, nos and nas: compraram plus o is compraram-no, dão plus a is dão-na, põe plus o is põe-no. After an oral vowel nothing changes: entreguei-o, disse-a. The l and the n are the same pronoun in different clothes, a consonant that makes the pronoun easy to say after the sound before it.

Mesoclisis has its own spelling. The infinitive stays whole, including its r, and the ending follows the pronoun: dar-lhe-ei, encontrar-nos-emos, ser-lhe-á. If the pronoun is o or a, the same lo and la rule applies to the infinitive: informar plus a plus emos is informá-la-emos, with the acute of case two. The stress falls on the ending, not on the pronoun, which stays weak (ser-lhe-Á). The irregular future stems shorten before the pronoun as they do without it: dizer gives dir-se-ia, fazer gives far-se-á.

Two commands also appear in this unit. The formal command of dar is dê, a stressed one-syllable word ending in e, so it takes the circumflex by the rule for stressed monosyllables, and it keeps the mark when the pronoun is attached: dê-me um minuto. The command dirija comes from dirigir with g changed to j to keep the zh sound before a (the commands unit), so Dirija-se ao balcão.

grammar.title: Combined pronouns and their colloquial substitutes
grammar.explanation:
A verb can have two clitic objects at once: an indirect object (the person who receives) and a direct object (the thing received), as in he gave me it. English handles this with a fixed word order (gave me it) or with a preposition (gave it to me). Written Portuguese fuses the two clitics into one word. The first pronoun loses its final vowel and the direct object o, a, os or as attaches to it: me plus o is mo, te plus a is ta, lhe plus os is lhos. The pattern is regular, with the indirect pronoun first and the direct pronoun second. The direct part agrees in gender and number with the thing, and the indirect part shows who receives it, so Deu-mo means he gave it (masculine) to me and Deu-ma means he gave it (feminine) to me.

The first and second person plural work slightly differently. Nos and vos lose their s and keep a hyphen before lo, la, los or las: nos plus o is no-lo and vos plus a is vo-la. This is the rule from the previous note, a final s dropping before lo and la, applied to the pronoun itself.

The forms with lh are ambiguous. Lhe (to him, to her, to you) does not show gender, and both lhe and lhes lose their endings before o, so lho can mean it to him, it to her, it to you or it to them, and only the context says which. That is one practical reason speakers abandoned these forms. Written, the combined forms are placed like any clitic: after the verb (Emprestei-lho), in front of it after an attractor (Ninguém ma contou) and inside a future (Dar-lho-ei). Because você is grammatically third person, writing uses lho for it to you, not the form to.

The combined pronouns belong almost entirely to legal, administrative and literary registers. In Brazilian speech they have disappeared, and speakers use three substitutes. First, they keep the indirect pronoun and drop the direct object when it is understood (Ele me deu, with the thing already clear from context). Second, they replace the indirect pronoun with pra or para plus the person (Emprestei pra ele, Entreguei pro Pedro, where pro is pra plus o). Third, they use the stressed pronoun as the direct object (Eu vi ele), which is normal in speech and avoided in writing. English has a faint parallel in the informal fusion gimme, but in Portuguese the fused forms are the formal ones.

Devolveu-lha logo. (he returned it to her at once)

grammar.title: The many functions of se
grammar.explanation:
Se is a clitic pronoun with the same shape in every role, but it does six different jobs, and the job decides how the verb behaves, above all whether it agrees with a plural noun. Do not confuse this pronoun with the conjunction se, which means if and is a different word that happens to be spelled the same: Se eu me queixar contains both, the first one meaning if and the second one the pronoun.

The way to read se is a chain of questions. First: does a subject act, and does the pronoun point back to that same subject? Then se is reflexive: Ela se olhou no espelho. Test it by adding a si mesma, herself (si is the stressed form of se, used after prepositions, like mim and ti). Second: is the subject plural, and do its members act on one another? Then se is reciprocal: Eles se abraçaram. Test it by adding um ao outro or mutuamente. A plural subject can be read either way (Eles se feriram could mean they hurt themselves or hurt each other), which is why speakers add mutuamente or a si mesmos to decide. Third: does the verb exist only with se, or mean something else without it? Then the pronoun belongs to the verb and se is inherent, which is the same as pronominal, a verb whose pronoun has no reflexive meaning: arrepender-se, queixar-se, atrever-se. Some verbs exist both ways with different meanings (lembrar and lembrar-se, encontrar and encontrar-se).

The remaining roles have no one acting on themselves. Fourth, passive se. A transitive verb, one that takes a direct object, can be used with se so that the thing becomes the subject and the verb agrees with it, as if it were the ser passive without an agent: Vendem-se casas means Casas são vendidas. The agreement is the test: one house is Vende-se casa and several are Vendem-se casas. Fifth, impersonal se. When the verb has no direct object (it is intransitive, or its complement needs a preposition), there is no noun to become the subject, so the verb stays in the third person singular whatever follows: Precisa-se de motoristas (precisar de), Trata-se de um erro, Vive-se bem aqui. This is the English one or people in one lives well here. It also combines with ser and an adjective: Quando se é jovem, tudo parece possível. Sixth, emphatic se: an optional reinforcement of a verb, often one of movement, with no change of meaning: Ele foi-se embora means the same as Ele foi embora.

In speech, Brazilians often avoid the passive and impersonal se. They use a third person plural verb (Vendem casas), a gente or você (A gente vive bem aqui, Aqui você precisa de carro). Many people also write Aluga-se apartamentos with a singular verb, but formal grammar treats it as an error, so write Alugam-se apartamentos when you write carefully. Signs, advertisements, laws and official notices keep the se forms, and inherent verbs keep se in every register. After an attractor the pronoun goes before the verb: Aqui se fala português.

grammar.title: Pronouns with ir plus infinitive and compound tenses
grammar.explanation:
When a verb comes in a group, an auxiliary plus a main verb, the pronoun has two candidates for its host. In Vou dizer-lhe the group has two verbs, but the pronoun is the indirect object of dizer, not of ir, so it belongs with dizer in meaning. English never faces the choice, since it puts the pronoun after the main verb (I am going to tell you). Portuguese allows several slots, and the rules depend on the kind of group.

Auxiliary plus infinitive (ir, querer, poder, dever, precisar and similar verbs). Formal writing puts the pronoun after the infinitive: Vou dizer-lhe, Quero vê-lo, Pode informar-me. The infinitive hosts the pronoun with the spelling rules of the previous notes (vê-lo, notificá-lo). Writing also allows it after the auxiliary (Vou-lhe dizer), but the infinitive is the usual choice in Brazilian writing. An attractor in front of the group pulls the pronoun before the auxiliary: Não lhe vou dizer, Nunca o quis ver.

Auxiliary plus past participle (ter plus participle: tinha dito, tenho visto). The pronoun attaches to the auxiliary, and never to the participle: Tinha-me dito, Tenho-me queixado, Tinha-o visto, never tinha visto-o. The reason is that a participle behaves like an adjective, as the participles unit showed, and adjectives cannot host a clitic. With an attractor the pronoun goes in front of the auxiliary: Não me tinha dito, Já o tinha visto.

Auxiliary plus gerund (estar plus gerund). A gerund is the verb form that ends in -ndo and says that an action is in progress (procurando, searching). It can host the pronoun, and nothing changes in the spelling: it ends in an oral vowel, so o stays o, and the stress does not move, so no accent is added (procurando-o, dizendo-lhe). After an attractor the pronoun goes before the auxiliary, as in the other groups: Não o estou procurando.

Everyday Brazilian Portuguese collapses all these options into one: the pronoun stands before the main verb, after the auxiliary, with no hyphen: Vou lhe dizer, Quero te ver, Tinha me dito, Tenho me queixado, Estou te procurando. Native speakers find this natural, even though traditional grammars label it incorrect. Use the formal position in exams, letters and contracts, and the colloquial one in conversation. For the third person direct object, speech also drops the object or uses ele and ela, as the object pronoun unit showed: Quero ver ele, where writing has Quero vê-lo.

culture.title: A gramática escolar e a fala brasileira
culture.text:
Pronoun placement is one of the clearest differences between written and spoken Brazilian Portuguese, and between Brazilian and European Portuguese. In Portugal, enclisis is the rule in ordinary speech: dá-me, disse-me, vejo-te amanhã. In Brazil, people say me dá, me disse and te vejo amanhã, and a sentence that begins with an enclitic pronoun sounds formal, even solemn.

The tension between school rules and real speech has a long literary history. In the 1920s, the Modernist poet Oswald de Andrade mocked the grammar book in a short poem called Pronominais, contrasting the textbook line Dê-me um cigarro with the everyday Me dá um cigarro. The point was to defend the Brazilian way of speaking as legitimate.

For learners, the practical lesson is to control both. Brazilian official and legal documents, academic texts, newspaper editorials and the questions on national exams such as the ENEM and public service tests keep the formal rules. The word juridiquês is used humorously for the heavily formal language of lawyers, with its mesoclisis, mo and lho. It is built like português and inglês, with the suffix -ês that names a language or a variety of one: the speech of the jurídico world. In conversation, however, insisting on dá-me may sound stiff. Choose the register to fit the context.

exercises.hint_source: They gave it to me yesterday.
exercises.explanation: Me plus o fuses into mo: the indirect pronoun comes first and loses its final vowel.

exercises.prompt: Which is the everyday Brazilian substitute for the written Entreguei-lho?
exercises.explanation: Speakers drop the combined pronoun and use pra plus the person, with the direct object understood from context.

exercises.prompt: In which sentence is se an inherent part of the verb?
exercises.explanation: Arrepender-se does not exist without se, so the pronoun belongs to the verb. The other sentences are reciprocal, reflexive and passive.

exercises.prompt: Which verb form follows the formal rule for a sign offering several apartments for rent?
exercises.explanation: Alugar takes a direct object, so se is passive and the verb agrees with the plural thing: Alugam-se apartamentos.

exercises.prompt: In Precisa-se de motoristas, why is the verb singular?
choices: Precisar takes a preposition, so se is impersonal and the verb stays singular
It is a mistake in the sentence
exercises.explanation: Precisar de takes a prepositional complement, so there is no direct object to become the subject and nothing for the verb to agree with.

exercises.prompt: Why is Tinha visto-o impossible in writing?
choices: Because o cannot follow a vowel
Because tinha is in the imperfect
A participle behaves like an adjective and cannot host a clitic, so the pronoun goes on the auxiliary: tinha-o visto
exercises.explanation: Clitics attach to verbs, not to adjectives. A participle works like an adjective, so the pronoun attaches to the auxiliary.

exercises.hint_source: I will send you (sir) the reply tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: With ir plus infinitive, formal writing attaches the pronoun to the infinitive.
Vender takes a direct object, so passive se is used and the verb agrees with casas.
Queixar-se is an inherent pronominal verb followed by de; reclamar needs no se.

exercises.prompt_source: I did not tell him anything.
answers: Eu não disse nada a ele.
Eu não disse nada para ele.
Eu não disse nada pra ele.
exercises.explanation: The negative word não attracts the pronoun in front of the verb in the formal version.

answers: A gente se encontra na sexta.
Nós vamos nos encontrar na sexta.
A gente se encontra na sexta-feira.
exercises.explanation: Encontrar-se is reciprocal here. The formal future uses mesoclisis; speech uses the present or ir plus infinitive with the pronoun in front.

exercises.prompt_source: I am addressing you, sir, to ask for information.
exercises.explanation: The verb comes first, so the pronoun trails it with a hyphen.

exercises.prompt_source: They did not tell me anything about this.
exercises.explanation: Não is an attractor, so the pronoun goes directly in front of the verb.

exercises.prompt_source: I commit to delivering the report.
exercises.explanation: Comprometer-se is pronominal, and the verb comes first, so the pronoun trails it.
The plural subject comes first and the reciprocal se stands before the verb.
Que is an attractor, so the pronoun stands before the verb of the dependent clause.

exercises.prompt_source: We will notify him in writing.
exercises.explanation: The infinitive hosts the pronoun: the r drops, o becomes lo and the last syllable takes an acute.

exercises.prompt: Which is the correct written form of abrir plus a?
exercises.explanation: The infinitive loses its r and a becomes la. The stressed last syllable ends in i, which the default for i already predicts, so no accent is written. The na form is only for nasal endings.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence places the pronoun correctly in formal writing?
exercises.explanation: Já is an adverb that attracts the pronoun, so it goes in front of the auxiliary. A participle never hosts a clitic, which rules out visto-o.

exercises.prompt: Why does Comprei o livro e entreguei-o ontem use enclisis after e?
choices: Because o always follows the verb
Because entreguei is a past tense
Because a coordinating conjunction such as e does not attract the pronoun, so the default enclisis applies
Because e is a negative word
exercises.explanation: Attractors are negatives, subordinating conjunctions, relative and question words and some adverbs. The conjunctions e, mas and ou only join clauses and do not pull the pronoun forward.

exercises.prompt: Why does the word ênclise always carry a written accent?
choices: It is a proparoxytone, and no ending predicts stress on the third to last syllable; the closed e takes the circumflex
It ends in e, which is always accented
The accent marks a nasal vowel
It separates ênclise from a verb form
exercises.explanation: ÊN-cli-se is stressed on the third to last syllable, and the closed e before n takes the circumflex, as in câmera.

exercises.hint_source: Go to the service counter (formal command).
exercises.explanation: The formal command of dirigir ends in a. A g before a would be the hard g of go, so the spelling changes to j, which keeps the zh sound.
Alugar takes a direct object, so se is passive and the verb agrees with the plural thing: alugam-se.

exercises.audio_target: Informo-lhe que o pedido foi deferido.
choices: I inform you that the request was rejected.
I inform you that the request was granted.
I inform you that the request was lost.
exercises.explanation: Deferido means granted; the rejected version would be indeferido.

choices: Apartments are rented in this neighborhood.
Apartments are being built in this neighborhood.
Apartments are sold in this neighborhood.
exercises.explanation: Vendem-se is the passive se of vender, to sell.

exercises.audio_target: Ela arrependeu-se de ter vendido a casa.
choices: She regretted having sold the house.
She regretted having bought the house.
She is happy she sold the house.
She wants to sell the house.
exercises.explanation: Arrepender-se de plus a past infinitive says what she regrets having done.
Lembrar-se de: the m before b marks a nasal vowel, and daquele is de plus aquele.
Não attracts the pronoun in front of the verb; esquecerei ends in the diphthong ei, so no accent is written.
The command dirija has j to keep the zh sound before a, and the pronoun trails the verb with a hyphen.

exercises.hint_source: We will inform you at once.
exercises.explanation: Informar plus a plus emos: the r drops before la, which leaves an acute on the last syllable of informá.

exercises.prompt: Match the combined pronoun with its meaning

pairs.source: te + a (her or it to you)
lhe + o (it to him or her)

exercises.explanation: The indirect pronoun comes first and loses its final vowel; the direct pronoun o or a attaches to it.

exercises.prompt: Match the administrative term with its meaning
exercises.explanation: Deferir does not mean to defer, and o protocolo is a receipt, not a set of rules.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence with the function of se
exercises.explanation: Reflexive: acts on itself. Reciprocal: plural subject, each other. Passive: the verb agrees with the thing. Impersonal: singular verb, no subject. Inherent: the verb requires se.
